NEW YORK, N.Y.


New York


— Bank of America today announced a $250,000


two hundred fifty thousand dollar


commitment to Tunnel to Towers Foundation, building on more than $160 million


one hundred sixty million dollars


in support for first responders, veterans and military service members over the past 15 years as the nation prepares to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks.


Beyond the new Tunnel to Towers partnership, Bank of America is expanding its support for organizations that preserve the history and legacy of September 11, including a $1 million


one million dollar


commitment to the National September 11 Memorial & Museum and funding for the National 9/11


nine eleven


Pentagon Memorial. The company is also supporting remembrance and service through 9/11


nine eleven


Day, New York-based first responder organizations and employee volunteer opportunities across the country.


*“September 11 is a deeply significant part of our shared history,”* said **[Brian Moynihan](https://newsroom.bankofamerica.com/content/newsroom/executive-bios/brian-moynihan.html) , chair and chief executive officer of Bank of America** . *“As we remember those who lost their lives and recognize all who responded in service and sacrificed so much, we are continuing our longstanding support for first responders, veterans, military service members and the organizations that serve them.”*


## Supporting Veterans through a new partnership with Tunnel to Towers Foundation


Bank of America is providing two hundred fifty thousand dollars


$250,000


to Tunnel to Towers Foundation to support new Veteran Villages offering housing and related services for veterans. The Veteran Villages are planned in 14 markets, including Buffalo, Charlotte, Detroit, Las Vegas, Long Island and New Jersey.


Bank employees will also participate in volunteer projects to assemble 3,000 “Welcome Home” care packages for individuals supported by Tunnel to Towers. Activities are planned in New York City; Washington, D C


D.C.


; Boston; Long Island; and New Jersey, in addition to the markets where the Veteran Villages will be developed.


*“As we approach the 25th anniversary of 9/11, we remember the heroes we lost that day and the brave men and women who answered the call to serve our country in the years that followed,”* said **Frank Siller, chairman and CEO of Tunnel to Towers Foundation** . *“Bank of America’s support for our Veteran Villages will change the lives of veterans who have struggled after returning home, providing them with a safe place to live and the support they need. We’re grateful for their commitment to make sure no veteran is left behind on the streets of the country they served.”*


## New exhibition at the National September 11 Memorial & Museum


- Bank of America is providing one million dollars


$1 million


as lead sponsor of the National September 11 Memorial & Museum’s new exhibition, In Their Honor: 25 Years of nine eleven


9/11


Inspired Service, exploring the unity, resilience and service inspired by September 11.
- This commitment brings Bank of America’s total support for the museum to more than twenty million dollars


$20 million


since its inception.

9/11


Pentagon Memorial

$100,000


in expanded support for the National nine eleven


9/11

$275,000


.

## New Chairs of Remembrance installation in Bryant Park


- Bank of America is sponsoring the Chairs of Remembrance in Bryant Park, near its offices which house more than 10,000 employees.
- The September 11 installation will feature 2,753 empty chairs, and employees and the public will be invited to place white carnations on them in remembrance of those who lost their lives.
- In connection with the Chairs of Remembrance installation, Bank of America will donate seventy five thousand dollars


$75,000


, divided equally among the FDNY Foundation, New York City Police Foundation and Port Authority PBA Widows’ and Children’s Fund.


## Commitment to 25,000 employee volunteer hours


- Bank of America employees have committed to completing 25,000 volunteer hours this year in support of first responders, veterans and military service members.
- More than 600 Merrill employees are expected to pack meals for local food banks in 23 cities as part of an annual day of service organized and led by the nonprofit nine eleven


9/11


Day, continuing Merrill’s nearly decade-long support of the organization.
- Through Wills for Heroes volunteer events in 12 markets, including Charlotte and 11 additional locations, employees and participating attorneys will prepare complimentary estate-planning documents for eligible first responders and their spouses or domestic partners.
- Employees will also participate in remembrance gatherings, moments of silence, care package projects and other service activities across the country.


## Additional activities in markets across the U S


U.S.


- **Long Island:** A commemorative blood drive with the New York Blood Center at firehouses and colleges from September 3 through October 27.
- **New York City:** Bank of America has provided one million dollars


$1 million


in support this year for the Intrepid Museum, which is also a[Museums on Us](https://about.bankofamerica.com/en/making-an-impact/museums-on-us-partners) partner. Additional activities include an employee commemoration gathering and a Tunnel to Towers 5K involving 500 Bank of America runners.
- **Greater Washington, D C D.C. :** “Welcome Home” kit assembly, a moment of silence and volunteer activities through nine eleven


9/11


Day, as well as participation in the National nine eleven


9/11


Pentagon Memorial gala and ceremonial groundbreaking for the Memorial Visitor Education Center.
- **Flight 93 National Memorial in Pennsylvania:** Bank of America helped bring this important memorial to life by supporting its completion.
- **Additional markets:** Employees in communities across the country, including New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, North Carolina and Maine, will participate in local commemorations, volunteer projects and community events.


## Frequently asked questions


### Question: Why is Bank of America announcing these commitments around the 25th anniversary of September 11?


**Answer:** Bank of America recognizes the profound significance of this milestone, which directly affected employees, including those who lost their lives, their families and people around the world. The anniversary is an opportunity to honor their memory, recognize first responders and members of the armed forces, and continue supporting organizations dedicated to remembrance, education and service.


### Question: How was the “more than one hundred sixty million dollars


$160 million


” figure calculated?


**Answer:** The figure represents Bank of America’s support over more than 15 years for organizations and programs serving first responders, veterans and military service members.


### Question: What is Bank of America’s new commitment to Tunnel to Towers Foundation?


**Answer:** Bank of America is providing two hundred fifty thousand dollars


$250,000


to support Veteran Villages in 14 communities. Employees will also pack 3,000 “Welcome Home” care packages for individuals supported by the organization.


### Question: How will Bank of America employees participate?


**Answer:** Employees will assemble care packages, pack meals for local food banks, take part in service projects and participate in remembrance gatherings and moments of silence. Employees have committed to completing 25,000 volunteer hours this year in support of first responders, military service members and veterans.


### Question: Are these commitments limited to New York and Washington, D C


D.C.


?


**Answer:** No. Programs and activities extend to communities across the United States, including Veteran Village locations in 14 markets, meal-packing events in more than 20 cities and local engagement in several additional markets.


### Question: What is Bank of America contributing to the three New York-based first responder organizations?


**Answer:** In connection with the Chairs of Remembrance installation in Bryant Park, Bank of America will donate seventy five thousand dollars


$75,000
